text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: multiple customer reports of TLS handshake failures to private endpoints in eu-west-1. Triggered at ~2026-03-14T10:12:01Z (thread root).

maddy: I'm on it — taking incident lead. grabbing context: customers see 502 / TLS handshake errors when calling our private routing layer.

alan: seeing the same in SRE dashboards, spike in 502 and CONNECT_FAIL on ingress. Alerts show NLB upstream errors.

ryan: I can pull logs from the private control plane. quick check: envoy logs show a lot of `tls: handshake failure` and `no certificates configured for server_name` around 10:11:30Z.

sara: paging netops in case this is peering/VPC related. @ryan any packet drops in host logs?

ryan: kernel logs on worker-3 show `IPTABLES DROP` for some flows, but also `ICMP frag needed and DF set` entries — looks like MTU/fragmentation suspects.

maddy: timeline so far: 10:06 routine cert rotation job kicked off in infra CI (scheduled). 10:09 deploy-bot reported completed for envoy-proxy group. 10:11 customers report errors. We might have a partial rotation state.

emily: we rotated certs on the LB and envoy, but there are still internal sidecars (legacy-proxy) that weren't part of the rotation job. Could be SNI mismatch.

alan: hypothesis list (working):
1) cert rotation out-of-sync -> clients get cert mismatch/handshake failure
2) MTU/fragmentation on VPC peering -> TLS handshake packets dropped due to DF bit -> handshake times out
3) routing/NAT rules changed -> some flows hit old path without certs

sara: let's triage quickly. I can run openssl from inside the VPC to the private endpoint.

sara: `openssl s_client -connect private-rt.eu-west-1.redwood:443 -servername private-rt.eu-west-1.redwood`
-- output snippet --
CONNECTED(00000003)
139776482299976:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert handshake failure:ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1543:SSL alert number 40
---
no peer certificate
---

ryan: that matches envoy logs. But openssl from the LB host shows a valid cert chain and CN matches. So something in between.

netops-bot: Noted VPC peering attachment p-abc123 had route table update at 2026-03-14T09:59Z. Attaching netops.

sara: running tcpdump on worker-3 during a repro attempt. capturing `tcp port 443 and host <client-ip>`
-- tcpdump snippet --
10:11:28.123456 IP client > private-rt: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
10:11:28.123789 IP private-rt > client: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1, win 65535, options [mss 1400], length 0
10:11:28.124000 IP client > private-rt: Flags [P.], seq 1:512, ack 1, win 64240, length 511
10:11:28.124500 IP private-rt > client: ICMP frag needed and DF set (mtu=1400)

maddy: that ICMP frag needed is key. MSS mismatch: client offered MSS 1460, server responded with 1400, then fragmentation needed. TLS handshakes can fail if initial packets containing ClientHello exceed path MTU and DF prevents fragmentation.

alan: confirmed: our peering link MTU is 1400 due to transit provider. The rotation changed the packetization? Unclear. But packet trace shows ClientHello got partially dropped.

ryan: to validate cert hypothesis I pulled the raw bytes from an upstream envoy instance that accepted the connection — it served the rotated cert. But the clients that fail never complete the handshake and no cert is logged. Points to MTU first.

emily: still need to check whether legacy-proxy without new certs is being hit by some traffic. Does any request route to legacy-proxy? route tables show some weight to legacy-10 group for canaries.

maddy: mitigation plan (short term):
- 1) reroute traffic away from peered path to a gw path with higher MTU (temporary) -> lowers frag risk. (alan/ryan)
- 2) set NLB to TCP passthrough for private-rt to avoid TLS termination differences until we confirm certs are fully rolled. (emily)
- 3) increase PMTU probe TTL/enable path MTU discovery retries? (netops)
- 4) rollback cert rotation if we detect mismatched certs on any route (maddy)

alan: executing step 1: updating route table to prefer direct-gw (higher MTU) for problematic prefixes. Will monitor.

ryan: changed NLB target group health check to use TLS on port 443 -> currently failing on some targets, passing on others. Passing ones are on newer envoy with rotated cert.

maddy: #live-doc: adding timeline + evidence as we go. Anyone paste the CI cert rotation job logs?

emily: pasted job logs: `infra-rotate-cert job #4521`
```
10:05:15 start job
10:06:02 rotate-envoy: success for shard-a
10:06:30 rotate-nlb: success for shard-a
10:07:15 rotate-legacy-proxy: skipped (tag mismatch)
10:08:45 finalize: success
```

maddy: aha — legacy-proxy skipped due to tag mismatch. That confirms hypothesis 1 partially: not all proxies rotated. But that only explains cert mismatch if traffic hits legacy-proxy. We still have MTU evidence. Could be a two-factor failure.

sara: collecting more logs: kernel on client-side shows retransmits and then connection reset with `tls: handshake failure`.

ryan: quick test: forced client to use smaller MSS: `ip route change ... mtu 1400` on a tester host and retried openssl -> handshake succeeded and cert presented.

maddy: that is decisive for MTU role. So root cause chain: cert rotation partially skipped + path MTU smaller than ClientHello size causing fragmentation -> for some flows the ClientHello is dropped (DF) before reaching the rotated envoy, so client never sees cert (appears as handshake failure). For other flows hitting legacy-proxy, even if ClientHello gets through, cert mismatch causes failure. Two independent but compounding issues.

emily: remediation steps (next):
- Ensure infra-rotate-cert job is updated to not skip pods due to tag mismatch (owner: infra).
- Run a one-off rotation for legacy-proxy across eu-west-1 (owner: emily).
- Adjust route preferences to prefer high-MTU path and open ticket with cloud provider to investigate peering MTU (owner: netops).
- Add MTU check to pre-rotation validation: `ping -s 1472 -M do` across peering attachments as smoke test. (owner: sres)

alan: rolling back rotation not required now — we'll instead finish rotating legacy-proxy and ensure MTU mitigations. Rolling back could reintroduce certs with shorter lifetimes.

maddy: customers: CS team drafting notification and temporary workaround (clients can set smaller TCP MSS or test with MTU 1400). I'll coordinate postmortem and customer comms.

ryan: logging saved: /var/log/infra/cert-rotate/4521.log and /var/log/packet-captures/1842004321-worker3.pcap.gz (linked in internal artifacts).

netops-bot: Ticket created NETOPS-789: Investigate peering MTU and route update at 2026-03-14T09:59Z.

sara: on-call handoff note for next shift: follow up on NETOPS-789, confirm legacy-proxy rotation succeeded, and validate no further 502/TLS spikes in last 30m.

maddy: incident status: mitigated (traffic routed away from low-MTU peering, legacy-proxy rotation in progress). Postmortem owners assigned: infra (cert-rotation fixes), netops (peering MTU), sres (add MTU smoke tests). Will run full RCA doc and distro.

ryan: final check: metrics trending down 10:40Z after route change. I'll keep watch and escalate if it flares.

emily: thanks all — great cross-team triage. :heart:

incident-bot: Incident update: SEVERITY: High -> mitigated at 2026-03-14T10:45:10Z. Postmortem scheduled for 2026-03-16.
